subject.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes

question: Which existing-skill updates may bypass explicit approval under the default automatic Skill Workshop policy?
rationale: Syntax cannot distinguish a complete rewritten skill from a frontmatter-valid plan document, so maintainers must choose the acceptable destructive-write boundary and UX tradeoff rather than encode an arbitrary similarity threshold.

options.title: Auto only non-destructive updates
options.body: Allow automatic creation and content-preserving additions, but require explicit approval whenever an update removes or replaces an existing substantive instruction line.

options.title: Keep similarity threshold
options.body: Retain the three-line and 50% classifier, explicitly accepting that sufficiently quoted plan documents can still auto-apply and documenting that risk.

options.title: Keep unconditional automatic apply
options.body: Remove the continuity override, retain only structural checks and summaries, and preserve the behavior established by the recent automatic-approval change.

recommendation.title: Auto only non-destructive updates
recommendation.body: Allow automatic creation and content-preserving additions, but require explicit approval whenever an update removes or replaces an existing substantive instruction line.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the automatic lifecycle approval behavior that the decision would narrow.
